answer: Each epoch, require every identity to revise one of its own earlier positions in light of fresh public evidence, naming what changed and why — a willow bends rather than snaps. The revision must cross a ridge: old and new claims cannot both stand, so graders can check the reasoning genuinely moves. At dawn the evidence set is new to everyone. A sybil operator running N clones must then author N distinct, coherent intellectual histories; one copied revision exposes a single mind, while faking N separate evolutions costs N minds' work.
